angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 691,090 km at 161.06 pc = 0.06 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 6.2087 +/- 0.0111 mas (same row, RUWE 1.04): 161.06 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.993374 solar radii from Lafarga et al. 2026, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-2518 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026MNRAS.548ag512L/abstract): 691,090 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.983 (0.943 to 1.023) from Gaia DR3 FLAME (Creevey et al. 2023, A&A 674, A26; astrophysical_parameters of the same source); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5751.2 K from Lafarga et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-2518 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026MNRAS.548ag512L/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Lafarga et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-2518 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026MNRAS.548ag512L/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-2518.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.436, rounded to two decimals
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-2518 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units 0.06615, from TICv8 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019AJ....158..138S/abstract)
ageSource: Gaia DR3 FLAME (Creevey et al. 2023, A&A 674, A26), astrophysical_parameters of Gaia DR3 5578799133210115328, flags_flame 00: age_flame 6.2580504 Gyr (16th to 84th percentiles 5.200592 to 7.316426)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
